title: App shell, routing & Electron wrapper
body:
## Context
CandleViewer is a single-page React + TypeScript app wrapped by an Electron desktop shell (primary surface for the owner; a plain browser over Tailscale is a fully supported surface for managers/viewers). Before any R1 charting screen can be built, the app needs the frame everything else mounts into: the React Router route tree of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2, auth- and RBAC-guarded routes (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4), the persistent global chrome SCR-010, the single global hotkey layer mandated by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1, the Electron main/preload process hardened to SR-110..SR-119 of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.11, and the system-state surfaces (offline, degraded, version mismatch, 404/403, crash) that every later epic reuses instead of inventing its own.

E10 sits at the end of the R0 dependency chain: `E05 --> E10` and `E09 --> E10` in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1, and it in turn gates `E10 --> E11` (chart engine core). Its roadmap scope line (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2) is: "React Router route tree per `12-sitemap.md`; auth-guarded and RBAC-guarded routes; Electron main/preload with `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, strict CSP, GPU flags tuned per E06; auto-update channel stub; env badge (Demo/Live) in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to local log". R0 exit criterion 9 is owned by this epic: "Electron shell boots the web app, passes a Playwright-Electron smoke test, and starts with the hardened security switches enabled (verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection)".

Story domain: **SET** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §27). The SET stories realised at *shell* level here are US-SET-002 (global hotkey layer, Must) and US-SET-009 (Electron shell preferences, Should); US-SET-001/003/004/005/006/007/008 belong to the later settings epic and E05, and are explicitly out of scope except for the shell hooks they need.

ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is the only non-`decided` ADR in the plan (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16). E10 therefore builds against Electron **behind a `ShellPort` abstraction** so the decision stays reversible, exactly as `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 instructs.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Goal** — a bootable, navigable, hardened application frame that every R1+ screen plugs into, with zero bespoke chrome per feature.

- **Routing**: `apps/web/src/routes/*` implementing every route ID R-001..R-903 of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 as declarations (real screens land in their own epics; E10 ships the tree, guards, loaders, error elements and placeholder route elements).
- **Guards**: auth guard, RBAC guard (Owner/Manager/Viewer), admin step-up guard (`/admin/**`, 30-min step-up TTL), deep-link param validation contract (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7).
- **Shell chrome**: SCR-010 App shell, SCR-011 Navigation rail & workspace switcher shell, SCR-015 Global toast host mount; components CMP-070 AppShell, CMP-071 NavRail, CMP-072 TopBar, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-084 GlobalSearchTrigger, CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-208 StatusBar, CMP-209 RightRail, CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-212 ToastHost.
- **Hotkeys**: the global hotkey/action registry, conflict engine and reserved-key policy (US-SET-002), plus `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/me/keymap`. The SCR-012 command palette and SCR-013 cheatsheet that consume the registry are **deferred to E15**.
- **Electron shell**: `apps/desktop` main + preload hardened per SR-110..SR-119, GPU flags from E06/ADR-0011, a single hardened `createWindow()` factory with minimal bounds persistence, and the auto-update channel **stub** (disabled until signing exists, SR-115). Multi-monitor state, system tray, SCR-027 pop-out windows and the US-SET-009 shell-preferences surface are **deferred to E15**.
- **System states**: SCR-153 degraded mode (CMP-092), SCR-155 not found (CMP-090), SCR-157 version mismatch (CMP-096, CMP-207, CMP-028), SCR-159 offline / shell-specific, 403 (CMP-089), global error boundary (CMP-091) with crash reporting to a local log.
- **Bootstrap**: `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`, WS topic `system` auto-subscription for health chips and env badge.
- Design (D), QA (Q) and Security (X) tickets carrying their own points.

**Children** (16 tickets, 39 pts): E10-D02, E10-D03, E10-D04, E10-K01, E10-T01, E10-T02, E10-T04, E10-T05, E10-S01, E10-S02, E10-S04, E10-Q02, E10-Q03, E10-Q04, E10-X01, E10-X02. E10-T05 (3 pts, added 2026-10-31 for #305's BQ-1 plan gap: the `/settings/hotkeys*` server half) keeps the epic inside the tolerance band (28.9-39.1).

**Exit criteria (epic-level)**
1. Every route in `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 resolves; unauthenticated access redirects to `/login`; RBAC-denied direct navigation renders `/403` (or 404 for `/admin/**`) and the corresponding API returns 403 with an audit row.
2. `/admin/**` is unreachable without a step-up token ≤30 min old; non-owners get 404 from the router.
3. The packaged Electron build asserts every SR-110 flag and every SR-112 CSP directive at build time; flipping any one fails CI (`electron-hardening` required check, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §9.4).
4. A Playwright-Electron smoke test boots the shell, logs in, reaches `/terminal` and asserts the DEMO/LIVE badge in every window including pop-outs.
5. Cold launch to interactive shell ≤3 s on reference hardware (budget #10, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3).
6. axe-core reports zero violations on SCR-010, 011, 012, 013, 015, 027, 153, 155, 157, 159 and the 403 surface.
7. One global hotkey layer exists, is remappable, detects conflicts, and refuses reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`).
8. No Bybit host appears in any CSP directive or in renderer-bundled code (SR-119 CI assertion).

**Risks**
- **R8 Browser/GPU compat** — GPU flags tuned for the reference machine may regress elsewhere; mitigated by the `degraded-2d` fallback (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` F15) and E06's `RenderProfile` probe.
- **R5 Scope** — the shell is a magnet for "just one more chrome element"; the component list above is closed for R0, additions go to R1 epics.
- **R10 Key-person** — Electron main-process knowledge concentrates in one engineer; mitigated by E10-T05 (architecture docs + ADR consequences) and a second `apps/desktop` reviewer via CODEOWNERS.
- ADR-0011 staying `proposed` past end of Sprint 03 would strand shell work; mitigated by the `ShellPort` abstraction (E10-K01) so a Tauri swap is a port implementation, not a rewrite.


### Scope reconciliation and descope register (2026-09-14)

E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 3 epic register; section 4.2; window S03-S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to **83 points** - 2.4x the allocation and far outside the +/-15% tolerance band (28.9-39.1). The R0 train has no room to absorb the difference: section 3.1 allocates 322 of 360 available points to E01-E10, leaving an 11% buffer that a 49-point overrun would consume twice over. Re-sizing the children without changing scope would have been a fiction, and raising the roadmap figure would have broken the train budget.

The epic has therefore been **re-cut to the roadmap scope line** - route tree and guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel stub; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary and crash reporting to a local log - which now decomposes to **36 points across 15 children**, inside the tolerance band. Everything removed is re-homed in a named existing epic; nothing is deleted, and **no R0 exit criterion is weakened** (criterion 9, the Electron hardening assertion and Playwright-Electron smoke test, is fully retained in E10-T02, E10-X02 and E10-Q02).

| Withdrawn | Was | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| E10-T03 window/monitor state, tray, SCR-027 pop-outs | 5 | **E15 Layouts & workspaces** (R1, S08-S09) | `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` section 6.2 keys pop-out and window state to the *layout*; E15 owns layouts. The roadmap-line auto-update stub and SCR-157 surface stay in R0, folded into E10-T02 and E10-S04. |
| E10-S03 command palette + cheatsheet | 3 | **E15** (R1) | Not in the E10 roadmap scope line. Both consume a populated command registry and symbol/route sources that only exist after E08/E11. E10-S02 still ships the registry they bind to, and reserves `Ctrl+K`. |
| E10-D01 shell UX research | 3 | **Split**: environment-legibility and panic-reachability studies folded into E10-D02; navigation card-sort and health-chip vocabulary to **E15** | The two studies that gate an R0 safety decision are kept in R0; the two that inform E15 surfaces move with them. |
| E10-D05 design-QA sweep | 3 | **E49 Defect burn-down & design-QA sweep** (R5); safety-signal subset folded into E10-Q03 | E49 exists for this pass. Badge and panic-control fidelity remain R0-blocking so no safety regression waits until R5. |
| E10-X03 abuse-case execution | 3 | **E43 Security hardening & pen-test remediation** (R4); scripted per-PR subset folded into E10-Q02 | E43 owns adversarial execution. The controls that must not regress per-PR are automated in R0 instead of being executed once. |
| E10-Q01 test plan and charters | 3 | Folded into **E10-Q02** | A separate planning ticket for a surface this size was ceremony; the plan is a deliverable of the suite that implements it. |
| E10-T05 architecture docs + ADR consequences | 2 | **E48 Documentation, runbooks & GA readiness** (R5) | E48 already owns "architecture and ADR index reconciled with the built system". The interim ADR-0011 position is recorded by E10-K01 so R0 loses no decision record. |

Remaining children were additionally right-sized against the reduced surface (notably E10-S02 registry-only at 2, E10-S04 at 2, and the QA/security tickets at 1-2 each), since each was originally scoped against the larger surface.

**Roadmap consequence**: no edit to `30-release-roadmap.md` is required - E10 now matches its published 34-point allocation within tolerance at 36. E15's allocation (34 pts, S08-S09) must absorb roughly 9 points of transferred scope and is flagged for review at R1 planning; E43, E48 and E49 absorb 3, 2 and 3 points respectively, all of which fit inside their existing reserves.

## Out of scope
- Screen content behind any route other than the shell surfaces listed above (charts, DOM, tickets, admin pages) — E11+ and E42.
- Settings screens SCR-110/111/113/116/117/118/119 themselves (US-SET-001/003/004/005/006/007/008) — later settings epic; E10 ships only the shell hooks (theme/density attribute application, keymap fetch, hotkey registry API).
- Workspace/layout persistence and the dock system (E15); E10 ships the nav-rail and workspace-switcher *shell*, not layout CRUD.
- Notification-centre content (SCR-014) — E40; E10 mounts CMP-209 RightRail only.
- Real auto-update delivery, code signing and release feeds — stub only (SR-115 keeps auto-update disabled until signing exists); real updates land in E48/R5.
- Android, any separate admin application, Tauri implementation work (measured in E06 only).
- Crash reporting to any remote service — local log file only.
- Window/monitor-state persistence, system tray, SCR-027 pop-out windows and the US-SET-009 shell-preferences surface - deferred to E15 (see descope register).
- SCR-012 command palette and SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet - deferred to E15; E10 ships the registry they consume.
- Full design-QA sweep (E49) and adversarial abuse-case execution (E43); R0 retains only the safety-signal and per-PR-regression subsets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued route resolves
  Given the app is built
  When an automated test navigates to each route ID R-001..R-903 from docs/plan/12-sitemap.md
  Then each route renders its route element or its documented redirect, and none renders the 404 fallback unintentionally

Scenario: RBAC-denied navigation is structural, not cosmetic
  Given I am signed in as a Viewer
  When I navigate directly to /admin/users
  Then the router renders 404, any data call returns 403, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Hardened Electron build
  Given a packaged production Electron build
  When the SR-114 build-time assertion suite runs
  Then contextIsolation, sandbox and webSecurity are true, nodeIntegration is false, the CSP matches SR-112 exactly, and no Bybit host appears in connect-src or in renderer bundles

Scenario: Cold start budget
  Given the reference hardware of docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md
  When the Electron app is launched cold 10 times
  Then app.whenReady() to "shell interactive" is <= 3 s at p95

Scenario: Shell survives a renderer crash
  Given a panel throws an uncaught render error
  When the global error boundary catches it
  Then the surrounding shell stays operable, a correlation id and copy-diagnostics action are offered, and the crash is appended to the local crash log
```

## Technical notes / design
- Router: React Router v6+ data router. In the browser build `createBrowserRouter`; in Electron the app is served from a registered custom `app://` protocol handler (not `file://`) so history routing, CSP `'self'` and `Origin` checks (SR-042) all behave.
- Guards are route `loader`s reading the `/me` bootstrap cache; the client check is **UX only** — the security boundary is server-side (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3, `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4).
- `ShellPort` (E10-K01) abstracts every Electron-specific capability: `windows`, `tray`, `updates`, `keychainHandle`, `crashLog`, `gpuInfo`, `notifications`. The browser build supplies a capability-reporting no-op implementation so shell-only settings are *hidden with an explanation*, never shown disabled (US-SET-009 "Browser build" scenario).
- Env badge derives from the backend-reported environment on `/me` and the WS `system` topic; never inferred client-side and never defaulted to DEMO (SCR-150 rule).
- Errors: RFC 9457 problem+json from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`version_conflict`, `step_up_required`, …) rendered by shared shell error surfaces.

## Test plan
Roll-up of children: unit (guards, hotkey conflict algorithm, ShellPort, deep-link validators), contract (`/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; WS `system` against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 `SystemUpdate`), integration (route matrix × role matrix), E2E (Playwright web + Playwright-Electron), perf (cold start, route change), a11y (axe + manual SR), security (hardening assertions, abuse cases). Coverage ≥80% on `apps/web` shell modules and `apps/desktop`.

## Security notes
Threat areas A-16 (Electron binary + auto-update) and AC-09 (Electron main process) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §3; STRIDE rows E1..E5 (§5.9) plus O11/U5 (renderer XSS abusing a live session). Controls: SR-110..SR-119, SR-042 (Origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site` allow-list including the Electron app origin), SR-049 (TLS; plain HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 for the host-local shell), SR-012 cookie flags, SR-025 step-up re-auth. Data classification: session cookies (SECRET) and user identity (PII); the shell must never hold Bybit key material (SR-119). `sec:review` label required on every PR touching `apps/desktop` or CSP.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA across all shell surfaces (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Landmarks (`header`/`nav`/`main`/`complementary`/`status`), CMP-085 SkipLink as first focusable element, `aria-current` on the nav rail, one global hotkey layer with reserved `Esc` and `Ctrl+K`, health chips expose state as words not colour, env badge announced on every route change, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured by every chrome transition, focus returns to the trigger when overlays close.

## Performance notes
Budget #10: cold launch to interactive workspace ≤3 s (Electron), ≤4 s (browser). Shell renders before workspace hydration; health chips update at 1 Hz and must never re-render the workspace subtree. Nav-rail expand/collapse ≤120 ms, transform-only, must not remount docked panels or drop GL contexts. Command-palette filter ≤16 ms over 2 000 entries. Toasts animate transform/opacity only.

## Observability
Structured logs via the E04 logger with redaction (never log cookies/tokens). Metrics: `shell_cold_start_ms`, `shell_route_change_ms`, `shell_ws_state`, `shell_crash_total`. Analytics/audit events from the screens catalogue: `command.executed` (name only, no payload), `help.hotkeys_opened`, `app.version_mismatch`, `app.update_applied`, `shell.offline_detected`, `shell.tailscale_unreachable`, `shell.gpu_unavailable`, `shell.window_restored`, `panel.floated`, `panel.redocked`. Correlation id propagated HTTP→WS per E04.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition (the descope register above is that record for the seven withdrawn tickets; each receiving epic must carry a linked ticket before E10 closes).
- [ ] Rolled-up child estimate is still within +/-15% of the 34-pt roadmap allocation at epic close; any drift is reconciled into `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` rather than absorbed silently.
- [ ] The eight epic exit criteria above verified end-to-end and evidenced on the ticket.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on `apps/web` shell modules and `apps/desktop`; no open P0/P1 bugs in E10 scope.
- [ ] `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `20-architecture.md` §2.1 C3 and ADR-0011 consequences updated to shipped reality.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on all shell routes + a manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: cold-start and route-change numbers recorded against budget #10.
- [ ] security: STRIDE model (E10-X01) finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Retro learnings filed as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- `E05` — design system v0 supplies tokens, themes and the atoms/molecules the chrome is assembled from (`E05 --> E10`).
- `E09` — auth/session/RBAC supplies the `/me` identity payload, session cookies and the step-up endpoint the guards depend on (`E09 --> E10`).
- `E02` — the `apps/web` / `apps/desktop` workspace packages and import-linter contracts.
- `E03` — CI jobs hosting the `electron-hardening`, `e2e-electron` and `a11y-axe` required checks.
- `E06` — GPU flags and the ADR-0011 interim decision the Electron build is configured from.
Interfaces relied on: `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`, `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`, WS topic `system`.

## Branch
`feat/e10-app-shell-*` per child ticket; PRs ≤400 LOC diff, one concern each (routing, chrome, hotkeys, Electron main, states).

## References
- `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` — route tree, RBAC mechanics, Electron window model, deep-link contracts
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-010..015, SCR-027, SCR-119, SCR-152..159
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-059, 070, 071, 072, 075, 076, 080, 084, 085, 089..092, 094, 096, 207..213, 215
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §27 SET — US-SET-002, US-SET-009
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` — rows US-SET-002, US-SET-009, SCR-010..015
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9, §6.11 (SR-110..SR-119), §9.4
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3, §4
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budget #10
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §2.1 C3, F15, §16
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2, §4.3, §11.1


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Wireframe app shell, nav rail, command surfaces and system states
body:
## Context
Low-fidelity structure for every surface E10 builds, resolved before pixels are spent. The screens catalogue already fixes the anatomy (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010 wireframe block, SCR-011..015, SCR-027, SCR-153..159) and the component inventory; these wireframes turn that prose into layout decisions that engineering can be estimated against, and they encode the E10-D01 findings.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
Wireframes (Figma file `CandleViewer — E10 Shell (Wires)`), one frame per state, at 1280x800, 1920x1080 and 2560x1440:
- **SCR-010 App shell**: top bar, nav rail, workspace canvas, right rail, status bar. States: normal, disconnected, degraded, frozen, lockout, read-only (viewer). Role variants owner / manager / viewer with the Admin entry absent for non-owners.
- **SCR-011 Nav rail & workspace switcher**: collapsed (icons) and expanded (labels); >20 workspaces with scroll + search; empty state.
- **SCR-012 Command palette**: empty query (recent + suggested), results grouped (navigate / panel / symbol / action / setting), no-results, RBAC-disabled entries with a reason.
- **SCR-013 Hotkey cheatsheet**: two-column grouped layout, conflict chip, printable variant.
- **SCR-015 Global toast host**: single, stacked, overflow, error (sticky) variants.
- **SCR-027 Floating panel window (Electron)**: title bar with panel/symbol/env, re-dock control, browser fallback notice.
- **System states**: SCR-153 degraded banner, SCR-155 404, SCR-157 version mismatch (non-blocking banner + blocking modal), SCR-159 offline / tailnet-unreachable / backend-unreachable / GPU-unavailable, the 403 surface (CMP-089) and the global error-boundary fallback (CMP-091) in both panel-level and route-level variants.

## Context
Shell motion sits on top of a GPU-saturated trading surface: a careless width or layout animation on the nav rail reflows the workspace and can drop a WebGL context mid-frame (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011 performance note). Motion must therefore be specified as a contract, not a vibe. The same pass closes the accessibility review of the hi-fi designs and produces the handoff package engineering consumes in Sprint 03.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables

Each entry gives property, duration, easing token and the reduced-motion substitute.
- **Reduced-motion spec**: the exact behaviour when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set or the in-app override from US-SET-007 is on — instant state change, no fade on heatmap or panels, no inertia.
- **A11y design review**: focus order per surface, keyboard-only route through the shell (skip link -> nav -> main -> right rail -> status bar), live-region strategy (polite for info, a separate `role="alert"` region for errors per CMP-212), announcement throttling for 1 Hz chips (CMP-076, CMP-208, CMP-210), reserved-key policy surfaced in the cheatsheet.
- **Handoff package**: Dev Mode links, token map, per-screen state matrix, the accessible-name string table, the analytics/audit event list per surface, and an open-questions log with named owners.
- Handoff walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will build E10-S01..S04.

```gherkin

  When the motion spec is reviewed against the hi-fi file
  Then every animated element has a property, duration, easing token and reduced-motion substitute, and no entry animates width, height, top or left on a region adjacent to a WebGL canvas

Scenario: Reduced motion is a first-class state
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then the spec defines an instant, non-animated result for every entry, and no entry degrades to "shorter duration" only

Scenario: Keyboard route is complete
  When the a11y review traces a keyboard-only path through the shell
  Then skip link, nav rail, main content, right rail and status bar are all reachable in a documented order, every icon-only control has an accessible name in the string table, and Esc returns focus to the invoking trigger for every overlay

Scenario: Handoff is accepted

```

Durations and easings are E05 motion tokens (`motion.drawer`, `motion.toast`), never hard-coded ms in component code. The accessible-name string table is delivered as a JSON file engineering imports, so names cannot drift between design and build.

Verified later by the built implementation: the a11y audit (E10-Q03) tests the documented keyboard route verbatim, and the perf benchmark (E10-Q04) asserts the nav-rail transition causes no layout of the workspace subtree.

Motion must never be usable to hide or delay a safety signal: the DEMO/LIVE badge and the disconnected banner appear immediately with no entrance delay, specified explicitly.

This ticket *is* the a11y design review: WCAG 2.2 AA focus appearance (2.4.11/2.4.13), no motion-triggered content (2.3.3), consistent help (3.2.6), and the `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 single-hotkey-layer and reserved-key rules reflected in the cheatsheet design.

Every motion entry must be compositor-only (transform/opacity). Explicit budget: no shell animation may add more than 1 ms of main-thread scripting per frame while a chart is rendering.

N/A — specification artefact.

- Prototype two implementations: `ElectronShellAdapter` (preload-backed) and `BrowserShellAdapter` (capability-false, no-op).
- Verify the preload bridge can satisfy the interface **without** a generic `invoke(channel, …)` (SR-111 forbids it) — i.e. every method is a named, typed, allowlisted channel.
- Record which capabilities a hypothetical Tauri adapter could satisfy and which would need redesign, as evidence for the ADR-0011 decision.

```gherkin
Scenario: Timebox is respected
  Given the 3-day timebox expires

```

## Technical notes / design
Sketch:

```ts

  floatingWindows: boolean; tray: boolean; autoUpdate: boolean;
  keychain: boolean; osNotifications: boolean; gpuInfo: boolean;
  reason?: Partial<Record<keyof Omit<ShellCapabilities,'reason'>, string>>;
}

  readonly capabilities: ShellCapabilities;
  windows: { float(paneId: string, route: string): Promise<void>;

  crashLog:{ append(entry: CrashEntry): Promise<void> };
```

R0 exit criterion 9 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) is explicit: "Electron shell boots the web app, passes a Playwright-Electron smoke test, and starts with the hardened security switches enabled (verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection)". `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §9.4 lists `e2e-web` and `e2e-electron` as required branch-protection checks. This ticket builds both suites and the shared fixtures every later epic will extend rather than reinvent.

It also produces the screenshot corpus that E10-D05 (design QA) and the visual-regression baseline consume, so capture conventions are fixed here once.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/desktop/e2e/` (Playwright-Electron) and `apps/web/e2e/` (Playwright web), sharing fixtures from a common package:
  - **Auth fixtures**: seeded owner / manager / viewer sessions with TOTP handled programmatically against the demo backend.
  - **Smoke (Electron)**: launch → login → reach `/terminal` → assert the DEMO/LIVE badge in the primary window; assert the SR-110 hardening flags and the SR-112 CSP at runtime; assert no Bybit host in any CSP directive.
  - **Windows (Electron)**: float a pane → assert a new window with the badge and the environment word in its title → close → assert re-dock; launch with a simulated missing display → assert restore onto the primary display.
  - **Routing & RBAC (web + Electron)**: parameterised over the route manifest × three roles, asserting rendered outcome incl. the admin-404 rule and the step-up modal.
  - **Hotkeys & palette**: `Ctrl+K` open/run, `Shift+/` cheatsheet, rebind→conflict→swap→persist-across-reload.
  - **System states**: forced panel crash, forced route crash, backend killed mid-session (offline), WS dropped (disconnect/reconnect), simulated GPU-unavailable.
  - **Screenshot corpus**: deterministic captures of every shell surface × theme × density for the visual-regression baseline and E10-D05.
- Flake controls: no arbitrary `waitForTimeout`, all waits on explicit conditions; a quarantine tag with a policy that a quarantined test must be fixed or deleted within one sprint.
- CI wiring into the `e2e-web` and `e2e-electron` required checks, with trace + video retained on failure.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-Q01:** a black-box test plan (`docs/qa/e10-shell-test-plan.md`) and a session-based exploratory charter set, scoped to the reduced E10 surface (routing and RBAC; chrome and states; hotkey-registry conflicts; system states; shell/browser parity). Charters target the two invariants: the environment badge is never absent or wrong, and a guard is never bypassable from the client.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-X03 (per-PR regression subset only):** scripted attempts that must re-run on every PR - direct admin-route navigation as manager and viewer, navigation with a stale `/me` after a server-side role downgrade, reaching `ipcRenderer` / `require` / `process` from the renderer, and suppressing the DEMO/LIVE badge via preferences, injected CSS or zoom. Each asserts that the control holds. The full adversarial campaign is E43.

## Out of scope
- The hardening *assertions themselves as a build-time gate* — E10-X02 owns the `electron-hardening` check; this suite asserts the same properties at runtime, which is the complementary check demanded by exit criterion 9.
- Performance measurement (E10-Q04).
- E2E for screens owned by later epics; this ticket ships the fixtures they will use.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Electron smoke passes in CI
  When the e2e-electron job runs on a pull request
  Then the packaged shell launches headlessly, logs in, reaches /terminal, and asserts the environment badge and every SR-110 flag at runtime

Scenario: Runtime CSP assertion
  When the smoke test inspects the loaded document
  Then the Content-Security-Policy matches SR-112, contains no unsafe-eval, and lists no Bybit host

Scenario: Pop-out round trip
  When a pane is floated and then closed
  Then a second window appeared carrying the environment badge and the environment word in its OS title, and after closing, the pane is back in its origin dock slot

Scenario: Role matrix is exhaustive and self-updating
  Given the route manifest gains a new route
  When the RBAC E2E runs
  Then the new route is automatically included, and the test fails if no expected outcome is declared for it

Scenario: Suite is not flaky
  When the suite runs 20 consecutive times on main
  Then the flake rate is 0 and any test that flakes is quarantined with a filed fix ticket within the same sprint
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Abuse regressions are caught per PR, not per release
  Given the scripted abuse subset absorbed from E10-X03
  When a change weakens a route guard or exposes a Node global to the renderer
  Then the e2e-electron required check fails on that PR with the offending control named
```

## Technical notes / design
Playwright's Electron driver launches the **packaged** build, not a dev server, so the assertions reflect the artefact that ships (dev-only relaxations would otherwise mask SR-114 violations — STRIDE E4). Hardening assertions read `webContents.getLastWebPreferences()` through a test-only main-process hook that is compiled out of release builds but present in the CI build, with the hook's absence in release asserted by E10-X02.

The RBAC matrix is generated from the route manifest (E10-T01) plus a declarative expectations table, so adding a route without declaring its expected outcome fails the build — the mechanism that keeps the matrix honest as the app grows.

Screenshots are captured with animations disabled, a fixed viewport set, a frozen clock and seeded data, so the corpus is deterministic enough to serve as a visual-regression baseline.

## Test plan
Self-testing: the suite runs 20× on `main` as an acceptance gate for this ticket, and trace/video artefacts are retained on failure. Coverage of the E10-Q01 plan is tracked explicitly — each automated case is tagged with the plan step it covers so manual regression effort can be reduced as automation grows.

## Security notes
This suite is the runtime half of the Electron hardening verification (exit criterion 9). Test credentials are demo-only, injected through environment variables from the CI secret store, never committed. The suite must never run against a live environment (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). Traces and videos can capture session cookies — artefact retention is limited to 7 days and the artefact bucket is access-controlled.

An axe-core scan is attached to each shell surface visited by the suite so a11y regressions are caught in the same run (feeding the `a11y-axe` required check); the formal manual audit remains E10-Q03.

The suite is time-boxed: `e2e-web` ≤8 min and `e2e-electron` ≤10 min so the R0 pipeline stays within the ≤15 min commit-to-dev budget (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 criterion 2). Tests run sharded and in parallel to stay inside it.

Failures attach trace, video, console logs and the correlation ids observed, so a CI failure is diagnosable without local reproduction.

title: Benchmark shell cold start, route change and chrome isolation against budget #10
body:
## Context
Budget #10 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3 is "Startup time (cold launch to interactive workspace): ≤3 s (Electron app launch → last-used workspace fully interactive, symbols subscribed) on reference hardware", measured by an "instrumented `app.whenReady()` → workspace ready event", and it is marked **Hard — R1 exit gate**. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13 restates it as ≤3 s Electron / ≤4 s browser to first chart frame.

E10 owns the portion of that budget before any chart exists, so it must establish the harness and the shell's share of the budget now — otherwise R1 inherits an unmeasured baseline and the gate becomes unenforceable. The second measurement here is subtler but just as important: the SCR-010 contract that 1 Hz health-chip updates never re-render the workspace subtree, and the SCR-011 contract that rail collapse is transform-only. Both are perf contracts that are easy to violate invisibly.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- **Cold-start harness**: instrumented Electron launch measuring `app.whenReady()` → main-process ready → first paint → shell interactive (bootstrap resolved, WS connected, chrome rendered). 10 runs, report p50/p95, on the reference hardware named in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- **Browser cold start**: equivalent measurement for the browser build against the ≤4 s budget.
- **Route-change benchmark**: p50/p95 for navigation between shell routes, including the lazily-loaded admin branch (first navigation includes chunk load).
- **Chrome isolation assertion**: automated render-count test proving zero workspace-subtree re-renders under 60 s of 1 Hz chip updates, and a DevTools trace proving the rail collapse produces no layout of the workspace and no GL context loss.
- **Palette filter benchmark**: ≤16 ms p95 over a 2 000-entry index across 100 keystrokes.
- **Multi-window GPU check**: with four GPU-heavy windows open, confirm the shell warns per SCR-027/SCR-046 rather than degrading silently (the ≥58 fps target itself is E11's to meet; E10 verifies the warning path).
- Committed harness runnable in CI with numbers recorded (not yet gating in R0, per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 Perf gate) plus a baseline file so R1 can enforce it.

## Out of scope
- Chart/engine frame-time benchmarks (E06/E11/E46).
- Backend API/WS load testing (E03/E45).
- Optimising anything — this ticket measures and reports; regressions become Bugs or Tasks against the owning ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cold start is measured, not estimated
  When the harness runs 10 cold launches on the reference hardware
  Then p50 and p95 are reported for each stage from app.whenReady() to shell interactive, and the totals are compared against the 3 s budget

Scenario: Browser build measured too
  Then the browser cold start is reported against the 4 s budget with the same stage breakdown

Scenario: Chip updates do not touch the workspace
  Given a mounted workspace subtree and 60 seconds of 1 Hz health-chip updates
  Then the workspace subtree records zero re-renders

Scenario: Rail collapse causes no layout
  When the nav rail is collapsed while a canvas is mounted
  Then the performance trace shows no layout of the workspace region, the transition completes within 120 ms, and no WebGL context-lost event fires

Scenario: Palette stays in budget
  Given a 2000-entry command index
  When 100 keystrokes are issued
  Then the p95 filter time is <= 16 ms

Scenario: Budget exceeded
  Given a measured cold start above 3 s
  Then the run is reported as a failure against the budget with the slowest stage identified, and a Task is filed against the owning ticket rather than the budget being adjusted
```

## Technical notes / design
Instrumentation points are emitted by E10-T02 (main-process timings) and E10-T04 (bootstrap and WS timings) as performance marks; the harness reads them via the Playwright-Electron hook and the browser Performance API, so the same event vocabulary is used in dev, CI and manual runs.

"Shell interactive" is defined precisely for this project as: chrome painted, `/me` resolved, preferences applied, WS `system` connected, and the first route element mounted. R1 extends the definition to "workspace fully interactive, symbols subscribed" — the extension point is documented so R1 does not silently redefine the metric and claim an improvement.

Render-count assertions use a test-only render counter injected around the workspace slot; it compiles out of production builds.

## Test plan
The harness is the test. It is run on the reference hardware manually for the authoritative numbers and in CI for trend detection (CI hardware is not the reference machine, so CI numbers are compared to a CI-specific baseline, never to the budget — a distinction recorded in the report to prevent false confidence).

## Security notes
No production data or live credentials; measurements run against staging (demo). Performance traces can contain URLs and user identifiers — traces are treated as internal artefacts with the same 7-day retention as E2E artefacts.

## Accessibility notes
Two a11y-relevant measurements: announcement throttling (1 Hz chips must not announce at 1 Hz) and the reduced-motion path, where transitions must be instant and must not merely be shortened.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the perf verification: budget #10 (≤3 s Electron, ≤4 s browser), SCR-011 ≤120 ms transform-only rail transition, SCR-012 ≤16 ms palette filter, SCR-010 chip isolation, SCR-027 four-window warning path.

## Observability
Emits `shell_cold_start_ms`, `shell_bootstrap_ms`, `shell_route_change_ms`, `palette_filter_ms` to the E04 metrics pipeline so the numbers are observable in Grafana in production, not only in CI — the same metric name in both places.

title: Render the persistent app shell chrome and navigation rail (SCR-010, SCR-011)
body:
## Context
SCR-010 is the page frame wrapping every authenticated route: "persistent identity of environment, account scope, connection health, navigation and global panic actions". It is the only surface a user sees on every screen, and it carries the product's two hardest safety invariants — the DEMO/LIVE badge that "is **always visible**, in every window, every layout tab, and cannot be hidden by any layout/theme setting" (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §1.1), and the panic controls that must be reachable deliberately and unreachable accidentally.

SCR-011 is the navigation rail and workspace switcher hosted inside it. Realises the shell half of US-LAY-005/006 and US-SET-002's host surface; the traceability matrix maps SCR-010 to US-LAY-005, US-PAPER-002, US-SET-002 and US-ADMIN-012, and SCR-011 to US-LAY-006 and US-SET-001.

This story ships the chrome and its states. Slots whose content belongs to later epics (account picker, recorder chip, notification list, workspace list) render as empty, labelled placeholders — the frame is complete even where the fill is not.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/shell/AppShell.tsx` composing CMP-070 AppShell, CMP-072 TopBar, CMP-071 NavRail, CMP-209 RightRail, CMP-208 StatusBar, CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-212 ToastHost (SCR-015 mount point).
- Top bar regions: environment badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal), connection status (CMP-076), health chips (CMP-210), global search trigger (CMP-084), user menu (CMP-061), symbol and interval pickers (CMP-219, CMP-220) as slots, account multi-select (CMP-105) as a disabled placeholder until E27/E28.
- Panic-button cluster (CMP-211 PanicButtons) rendered with its confirm treatment wired but its actions routed to a not-yet-available handler in R0 — the control exists, is correctly gated and audited-by-construction via CMP-093, and reports "trading not enabled in this build" rather than silently doing nothing.
- Status bar: WS latency, clock with UTC label, bar-close countdown slot, version string; values fed from the E10-T04 store at 1 Hz.
- Nav rail (SCR-011): items Terminal, Watchlist, Positions, Risk, Rules, Replay, Journal, Alerts, Settings, and **Admin hidden entirely for non-owners**; collapsed (icon) and expanded (label) variants with a pin toggle; badge counts as slots; `aria-current` on the active item.
- Shell states from the catalogue: normal, disconnected, degraded, frozen, lockout, read-only (viewer). Role variants owner / manager / viewer.
- Route-change behaviour: focus moves to the main landmark heading and the environment badge is announced.
- Storybook stories for every state × role × theme.

## Out of scope
- Workspace list content, workspace CRUD, drag-to-reorder and layout loading (E15) — the switcher renders a placeholder list.
- Notification-centre content (SCR-014, E40) — CMP-209 RightRail is mounted empty.
- Account picker data and trade-group scope (E27/E28) — placeholder, disabled with an explanation.
- Recorder chip data (E16) — chip reports "not available in this build".
- The actual flatten/freeze/kill-switch behaviour (E39) — routed, not implemented.
- Command palette and hotkey cheatsheet — E10-S03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Environment badge is unconditionally visible
  Given any authenticated route, theme, density or layout
  When the shell renders
  Then the DEMO or LIVE badge is present in the top bar, and no theme, density, layout or user preference can remove it

Scenario: Admin is absent, not disabled, for non-owners
  Given I am signed in as a Manager
  When the nav rail renders
  Then no Admin entry exists in the DOM at all, and the accessibility tree contains no Admin item

Scenario: Viewer sees a structurally read-only shell
  Given I am signed in as a Viewer
  Then mutating controls including the panic cluster render in their disabled-with-reason treatment, each exposing an explanation such as "Viewers cannot place orders"

Scenario: Disconnected state
  Given the WS connection drops
  Then the top bar switches to its warning treatment naming the last-data age, the state is announced once via role=alert and not re-announced on every heartbeat, and the panels retain their last-good timestamp

Scenario: Health chips do not disturb the workspace
  Given a chart is rendering in the workspace
  When the health chips update at 1 Hz for 60 seconds
  Then the workspace subtree performs zero re-renders, verified by a render-count assertion

Scenario: Nav rail collapse is cheap
  When I collapse the nav rail
  Then the transition completes within 120 ms, uses transform only, and no docked panel is remounted and no WebGL context is lost

Scenario: Keyboard entry into the shell
  When I press Tab on a freshly loaded route
  Then the first focusable element is the skip link, activating it moves focus to the main landmark, and the nav rail is reachable with a documented focus order
```

## Technical notes / design
The shell subscribes to the E10-T04 store with selector-level granularity: chip values live in a store outside the workspace React tree and are rendered through subscriptions, never through a context that would propagate a re-render into the workspace subtree — this is the mechanism that makes the "zero workspace re-renders" acceptance criterion achievable rather than aspirational.

Role variance is **structural**: nav items are filtered from the item array before render, so a hidden item cannot be revealed by DOM inspection or a CSS override. This mirrors the server-side guarantee in `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4 that a Viewer never receives out-of-scope payloads.

The nav-rail collapse animates `transform: translateX` on the rail plus a CSS grid column width driven by a container query fallback; width animation is explicitly forbidden by the SCR-011 performance note because it reflows and would drop GL contexts.

Slots for later-epic content are typed React slots with a documented `NotAvailableYet` fallback so the epic that owns the content fills a contract rather than editing the shell.

## Test plan
- Unit: role-based nav item filtering (owner/manager/viewer); state machine for normal/disconnected/degraded/frozen/lockout/read-only; badge presence invariant under every theme and density.
- Component/render-count: workspace subtree render count under 60 s of 1 Hz chip updates.
- a11y: axe-core on every state × role; keyboard-order test asserting skip link is first focusable; announcement test for route change and for the disconnected transition.
- Visual regression: Storybook snapshots for every state × role × theme × density.
- E2E: login → shell renders → navigate between three routes asserting `aria-current` and the announced badge.

## Security notes
The badge invariant and the structural Admin hiding are safety/security controls, not styling: a test asserts the badge cannot be removed by any preference, and another asserts the Admin item is absent from the DOM for non-owners. The panic cluster is wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger so that when E39 lands, every invocation is audited by construction. Client-side role filtering is explicitly documented in code as a UX affordance, with the server-side 403 as the real boundary (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3). Data classification: displays the user's name and role (PII) — not logged, not persisted.

## Accessibility notes
Landmarks: `header` (top bar), `nav aria-label="Primary"` (rail), `main`, `complementary` (right rail), `role="status"` (status bar). CMP-085 SkipLink is the first focusable element. `aria-current="page"` on the active nav item; active state is not colour-only. Health chips expose "label: state, value" as their accessible name — state is always a word. The environment badge is announced on every route change. Badge counts are part of the accessible name ("Alerts, 2 new"). Collapsed rail icons have always-present `aria-label` plus a keyboard-reachable tooltip. Verified against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.

## Performance notes
Shell renders before workspace hydration (SCR-010 note). Health chips update at 1 Hz and never re-render the workspace subtree. Rail expand/collapse ≤120 ms, transform-only, no panel remount, no GL context loss (SCR-011 note). Contributes to budget #10 (≤3 s cold start): the shell's first paint is the milestone the cold-start metric measures against.

## Observability
Events: `session.account_scope_changed` (audited, when E27 lands), `workspace.opened` (analytics, when E15 lands) — the emitters are wired now with typed payloads so later epics do not re-plumb them. Metric `shell_first_paint_ms` feeding `shell_cold_start_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass, each mapped to a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: touched frontend package lines >=80% (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2); no regression to the package baseline.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` amended if shipped behaviour diverged from spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched surfaces; keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E10-D03 hi-fi spec by a designer (tracked on E10-D05); deviations fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*`.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario.
- [ ] Storybook entries added/updated for every touched component with all documented states.
- [ ] Changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), never live.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, 2 approvals incl. a code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (flag key + default per environment).

## Dependencies
- `E10-T01` — the root route element that hosts the chrome.
- `E10-T04` — the bootstrap store supplying identity, environment, preferences and health.
- `E10-D04` — signed-off hi-fi + motion + a11y handoff (design-ahead: Done in Sprint 02).
- `E05-S01` — the atoms/molecules and theme runtime the chrome composes from.
Blocks `E10-S02`, `E10-D05`.

**Design-ahead waiver (recorded per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1).** The design-ahead rule wants a consuming Story to start >=2 sprints after its design ticket is Done. E10's hi-fi pack (E10-D03) and handoff (E10-D04) complete in Sprint 02 and E10-S01 starts in Sprint 03 - a one-sprint gap. The gap cannot be widened: Sprint 01 is the first sprint of the programme, so no E10 design ticket can land earlier, and E10 must complete in R0 (S03-S04) because `E10 --> E11` gates the entire R1 chart-engine train. The waiver is granted on the condition that the shell is assembled from already-signed-off E05 design-system components rather than novel visual work, which is what makes a one-sprint gap tolerable here. title: Implement the global hotkey registry with remapping and conflicts (US-SET-002)
body:
## Context
US-SET-002 (Must) — "As a trader, I want one remappable hotkey scheme across every view, so that muscle memory always works" — with the explicit NFR "one hotkey layer, not per-view schemes (explicit design requirement)". `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1 restates it as a conformance rule: a single global layer governs the whole app, no view silently overrides a global binding, view-local hotkeys are additive and active only while their view has focus.

§3.3 fixes the conflict algorithm and the non-negotiable constraints: global bindings cannot be overridden by view-local ones; trading-critical bindings (submit, cancel, flatten) cannot be bound to an unmodified single letter; `Esc` and `Ctrl+K` are permanently reserved and excluded from the remap UI — `Ctrl+K` specifically because it is the recovery mechanism if a user breaks their own hotkey config.

Bindings are persisted in the `hotkey_profiles` Postgres table (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.5), which already models one global layer per user (`bindings jsonb`, `scheme_base`, `requires_arm`), and read by the shell through `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/shell/hotkeys/registry.ts`: a single registry where every action registers `{id, label, group, defaultKeys, focusContexts, dangerous}`; resolution is global-first with view-local bindings additive and scoped to focus context.
- Binding resolution engine honouring `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2 defaults: `Ctrl+K` command palette, `Ctrl+\` region focus cycle, `/` watchlist/symbol search (inert inside text inputs), `Shift+/` cheatsheet, `Alt+1..9` nav rail, `F11` full-screen workspace, `Ctrl+Shift+A` account picker.
- Conflict detection per §3.3: on a rebind attempt compute the new combo's active focus-context set; if it intersects an existing binding's context set for a *different* action, block the save, show both actions and offer a one-click swap.
- Guard rails: reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`) refused with a stated reason; trading-critical actions refused an unmodified single letter; OS/browser-reserved combinations refused with the reason (US-SET-002 "Reserved keys" scenario).
- Inert-with-explanation behaviour: a binding pressed in a view where its action is invalid explains why on press rather than doing nothing (US-SET-002 "Remap" scenario).
- Profile plumbing: read the active profile from `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`, persist changes through `PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences`; export/import of a profile as JSON (NFR "profiles exportable").
- Arm-toggle awareness: `hotkey_profiles.requires_arm` is respected — trading hotkeys are inert unless armed (the arm control itself lands with E30; the registry honours the flag now).

## Out of scope
- The hotkey editor screen SCR-113 (`/settings/hotkeys`, R-202) — later settings epic; this story exposes the registry API and the conflict engine it will consume.
- Trading, chart, DOM and rule-editor action *implementations* — they register their actions in their own epics; E10 ships the registry plus the shell's own actions.
- The cheatsheet and command-palette surfaces — E10-S03.

- SCR-012 command palette and SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet - **deferred to E15**. This story ships the registry, the conflict engine, the reserved-key policy and the `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/me/keymap` plumbing that E15 consumes; `Ctrl+K` is reserved here and wired to a no-op until E15 mounts the palette on it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One layer, not per-view schemes
  Given the same binding is requested by a global action and a view-local action
  When the view has focus
  Then the global binding wins, the view-local registration is rejected at registration time with a developer-facing error, and no silent override occurs

Scenario: Remap applies everywhere the action is valid
  Given I bind Ctrl+Shift+F to flatten
  When I press it in any view where flattening is valid
  Then the action runs; and where it is not valid it is inert and explains why on press

Scenario: Conflict must be resolved before saving
  Given Ctrl+Shift+F is already bound to another action in an intersecting focus context
  When I attempt the rebind
  Then the save is blocked, both actions are named, and a one-click swap is offered

Scenario: Reserved keys are refused
  When I try to bind Esc or Ctrl+K
  Then the bind is refused with the stated reason, and neither appears as remappable in the registry metadata

Scenario: Trading actions need a modifier
  When I try to bind flatten to the single letter F with no modifier
  Then the bind is refused with the accidental-trigger reason

Scenario: Typing is never hijacked
  Given focus is inside a text input
  When I press "/"
  Then the character is typed and the symbol-search binding does not fire

Scenario: Profiles round-trip
  When I export my profile and import it into a clean profile
  Then every binding is restored identically and the import reports any binding that is invalid in the current build rather than dropping it silently
```

## Technical notes / design
Resolution model: each action declares a `focusContexts: string[]`. At key-down the engine computes the active context stack from the focused element's nearest context provider, then resolves global bindings first and view-local bindings only if the context matches. Conflict detection is set intersection over context sets — the algorithm is specified verbatim in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.3 and must be implemented as written, including the dual-meaning display rule (when editing `+`/`-` the UI shows both the chart-zoom and ladder-zoom bindings side by side, because mutually exclusive contexts are not a conflict but are confusing).

Key normalisation handles layout differences (`event.code` for physical keys, `event.key` for characters) so a binding survives a keyboard-layout change; this is recorded as a known limitation area with unit tests for the QWERTY/AZERTY cases.

Persistence: `hotkey_profiles.bindings` is a jsonb map of `action_id -> string[]`; the client sends a full profile on save (small payload, avoids merge races) and the server validates against the closed action vocabulary.

## Test plan
- Unit: resolution precedence (global vs view-local); conflict set-intersection across representative context sets; reserved-key refusal; single-letter refusal for `dangerous` actions; text-input inertness; key normalisation across layouts.
- Contract: `GET /api/v1/me/keymap` response and `PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences` payload against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Integration: registry rejects a view-local registration that collides with a global binding.
- E2E: rebind → conflict → swap → persisted across reload; export/import round-trip.
- a11y: rebind flow operable by keyboard only, with the live-region announcements specified by CMP-064.

## Security notes
Hotkeys can trigger destructive and money-moving actions, so the registry is a safety surface: `dangerous` actions require a modifier, honour `requires_arm`, and always route into their confirm flow (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-003 policy) rather than executing directly from a keypress. Imported profiles are untrusted input — validated against the closed action vocabulary, with unknown action ids rejected and reported, never executed. No key material or PII is stored in a profile.

## Accessibility notes
This story is a direct `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 conformance item. `Ctrl+K` must remain permanently reserved as the recovery escape hatch. The rebind control announces "press new key combination" then confirms or reports the conflict via a live region (CMP-064 contract). Every binding must have a non-keyboard equivalent path (menu, command palette) so the app is never keyboard-only-operable-by-memory. Single-key bindings are only permitted for non-destructive actions and must be suppressible, per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts.

## Performance notes
Key-down resolution is O(1) via a precomputed combo→action map rebuilt only on profile change; resolution must add no measurable latency to the input path (<1 ms) so trading hotkeys stay instantaneous. The listener is a single document-level handler, not one per component.

## Observability
Events: `hotkey.rebound {action, from, to}` (analytics), `hotkey.conflict_blocked {action, collidesWith}` (analytics — a high rate here is a design signal), `hotkey.inert_pressed {action, view}` (analytics, tells us where users expect an action that is not valid). Never log the key sequence alongside identifying data in a way that could reconstruct typed content.

title: Implement the system-state surfaces: 403, 404, degraded, offline, crash boundary
body:
## Context
Every later epic needs somewhere to land when things go wrong, and the catalogue already specifies those places precisely: SCR-153 degraded mode, SCR-155 not found, SCR-159 offline / shell-specific states, plus the 403 surface (CMP-089) and the global error-boundary fallback (CMP-091). Building them once in the shell is what stops fifteen epics inventing fifteen different "something went wrong" screens.

Two rules dominate the copy and behaviour. First, reassurance must be accurate: the disconnected and crash surfaces say "your positions are unaffected and protected by native stops" **only where that is true** — the native exchange-side SL invariant is real (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` locked decisions), so the statement is meaningful and must not be shown in contexts where it would be false. Second, offline detection is driven by actual request failure rather than `navigator.onLine`, so a connected-but-unreachable tailnet is named as such within 5 s (SCR-159 performance note).

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- **403 / Forbidden** (route R-900, CMP-089 ForbiddenState): shown for RBAC-denied direct navigation, with the reason and a route back to something the user can reach.
- **404 / Not found** (route R-901, SCR-155, CMP-090 NotFoundState): includes the attempted path.
- **SCR-153 Degraded mode** (CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner): a banner for each impairment class — exchange WS down → REST polling; recorder down → no new history; rule engine down → armed rules not evaluating; GPU fallback → reduced visual fidelity. Each names the impairment, what still works, and what does not. Dismissible per issue but reappears while the condition persists.
- **SCR-159 Offline / shell-specific states**: browser offline, tailnet unreachable ("Not connected to the tailnet"), backend unreachable at boot (retry with a diagnostic checklist), and the Electron GPU-process-crash recovery state naming the fallback and its limitations.
- **Global error boundary** (CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback) in two variants: panel-level (surrounding UI survives) and route-level; each offers a correlation id, a copy-diagnostics action, and reload-panel vs reload-app; a repeated-crash state stops auto-remounting and explains why.
- **Crash reporting to a local log**: crashes appended to a local file through `ShellPort.crashLog` in Electron and buffered in memory in the browser, with secrets redacted; surfaced by the diagnostics-copy action.
- Shared copy module so every surface's wording is reviewed once and reused, rather than being retyped per epic.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-T03:** **SCR-157 version mismatch** (CMP-028 banner non-blocking / blocking modal, CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel, CMP-207 BuildFooter), driven by the E10-T02 version check. "Incompatible" blocks trading-capable surfaces only; read-only views remain usable. This is the renderer surface only - the channel abstraction itself is E10-T02.

## Out of scope
- SCR-152 disconnected/reconnecting banner's *reconnection logic* — implemented in E10-T04; this story renders the surfaces it drives.
- SCR-157 version mismatch — E10-T03.
- SCR-158 rate-limited state — E34/E29 own the rate-limit semantics.
- Remote crash reporting or any third-party telemetry service — local log only, deliberately.
- Maintenance mode (R-903) content — E42.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Forbidden navigation lands somewhere useful
  Given I am a Manager and I navigate directly to a route I may not access
  When the 403 surface renders
  Then it states why access was denied and offers a link to a route I can reach, and the corresponding API call returned 403 with an audit row

Scenario: Tailnet unreachable is named precisely
  Given navigator.onLine reports true but every backend request fails
  When 5 seconds have elapsed
  Then the offline state names the tailnet/backend reachability condition specifically, rather than showing a generic "you are offline" message

Scenario: Degraded mode is honest about scope
  Given the exchange WS is down but the backend is healthy
  Then the degraded banner names the impairment, states that data is now polled, lists what is unavailable, and does not imply the whole app is broken

Scenario: Panel crash does not take down the shell
  Given one panel throws during render
  Then only that panel is replaced by the panel-level fallback, the shell and every other panel stay interactive, and a correlation id plus copy-diagnostics action are offered

Scenario: Repeated crashes stop the loop
  Given the same panel crashes three times within one minute
  Then auto-remounting stops, the surface explains why, and the user is offered reload-app as the next step

Scenario: Reassurance is only shown when true
  Given the app is disconnected while positions are open and carry native exchange-side stops
  Then the surface states that exchange-side stops are unaffected; and in any context where that guarantee does not hold, the statement is absent

Scenario: Diagnostics contain no secrets
  When I use copy-diagnostics
  Then the payload contains version, build hash, correlation ids, recent log lines and settings, with cookies, tokens and any key material redacted
```

```gherkin
Scenario: An incompatible client blocks trading surfaces but not read-only ones
  Given the backend reports a protocol version this client cannot speak
  When the version check completes
  Then SCR-157 renders a blocking modal over trading-capable surfaces
  And read-only views remain usable, and the build footer shows both versions
```

## Technical notes / design
The error boundary is a React error boundary at two levels: one wrapping each panel slot and one wrapping the route outlet, both reporting through a single `reportCrash()` that assigns a correlation id, appends to the crash log and increments `shell_crash_total`. The repeated-crash guard is a per-boundary counter with a one-minute sliding window.

Degraded-mode issues are derived from the WS `system` payload (E10-T04) rather than from ad hoc per-feature flags, so a new impairment class is a payload addition, not a new banner implementation.

Offline detection: a lightweight liveness probe plus observed request failures; `navigator.onLine` is used only as a fast-positive hint and never as the sole signal (SCR-159 note).

Diagnostics redaction reuses the E04 redaction filter list so the client and server agree on what is never emitted.

## Test plan
- Unit: degraded-issue derivation from `SystemUpdate` payloads; repeated-crash window logic; redaction of the diagnostics payload against a fixture containing a cookie, a bearer token and a key-like string.
- Integration: offline detection within 5 s under a "online but unreachable" network stub; 403/404 routing.
- E2E: throw in a panel → panel-level fallback, shell still interactive; throw in a route → route-level fallback; disconnect drill showing the banner and the accurate reassurance copy.
- a11y: axe on every state; `role="alert"` announced once for the offline transition; headings and named actions on each surface.
- Chaos (with E10-Q02): kill the backend mid-session; simulate a GPU-process crash in Electron and assert the documented recovery state.

## Security notes
The diagnostics bundle is the main risk surface: it must never contain cookies, bearer tokens, API keys or the KEK handle (SR-122 "never log tokens"; SR-119). A unit test asserts redaction against a fixture of known-sensitive shapes. The 403 surface must not disclose the existence or contents of resources the user may not see — it states the denial, not the target's details. Crash logs are written to the user's local machine only and are never transmitted.

## Accessibility notes
Each state is a page or banner with a heading and a plain sentence; nothing relies on OS-level chrome. `role="alert"` once on the offline transition, then a persistent banner; countdowns are not announced on every tick. Severity is encoded by icon + text, never colour alone. The error-boundary fallback exposes the correlation id as selectable text and the copy action as a named button. The GPU-unavailable state names the fallback and its limitations in words.

## Performance notes
Offline detection within 5 s of an unreachable backend. The error boundary must not itself be expensive: the fallback is a static component with no data fetching. Degraded banners must not re-render the workspace subtree — they mount in the chrome layer, consistent with the SCR-010 isolation rule.

## Observability
Events: `shell.offline_detected {cause}`, `shell.tailscale_unreachable`, `shell.gpu_unavailable`, `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}`, plus an incident-log entry for crashes affecting a trading surface (raised at high severity per the catalogue). Metrics: `shell_crash_total` labelled by boundary level, `shell_degraded_active` gauge per impairment class.

- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass, each mapped to a named automated test.
