title: Implement the route tree, auth/RBAC/step-up guards and deep-link validation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 is the single source of truth for the route tree: 60+ route IDs from R-001 `/login` to R-903 `/maintenance`, each with an RBAC column (`O`/`M`/`V`/`A`, `◑` scoped, `⓪` read-only). §4 fixes the gating mechanics: every route is enforced twice — a router loader checks client-cached claims for UX, and every API call is independently authorised server-side; the client check is *never* the security boundary. §7 fixes the deep-link parameter contract (`symbol`, `tf`, `paneFocus`, `panel`, `account`, `groupBy`, `showClosed`, `from`, `to`, `speed`, `fromReplay`, `mode`, `standalone`) with validation rules per param.

Without this, every later epic invents its own routing and guard logic, and the `/admin/**` step-up rule (30-min TTL) gets implemented three different ways.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/routes/tree.tsx` declaring every route ID R-001..R-903 from `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2, with the documented redirects (`/` → `/login` or `/terminal`; `/terminal` → `/terminal/:layoutId`; `/settings` → `/settings/profile`; `/` → `/login/first-run` when zero users exist).
- Placeholder route elements for routes owned by later epics, each rendering a labelled "owned by <Epic>" stub so the tree is complete and testable now.
- `requireAuth` loader: redirects unauthenticated users to `/login` preserving the intended destination.
- `requireRole(roles)` loader: renders `/403` (CMP-089 ForbiddenState) for denied non-admin routes; `/admin/**` denials render **404** for non-owners per `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 note.
- `requireStepUp` loader for `/admin/**`: 30-min TTL; on expiry surfaces the M-020 step-up modal contract and calls `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`; handles the `step_up_required` problem+json type from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Deep-link validators per `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7, one per param, with the documented fallbacks (invalid `symbol` → toast + last symbol; invalid `tf` → 15; `speed` clamped 0.5–100).
- Route-level `errorElement` wired to the global error boundary (E10-S04).
- A generated route manifest (`apps/web/src/routes/manifest.ts`) used by the command palette (E10-S03) and by the E10-Q01 route-matrix test.

## Out of scope
- Screen content for any route owned by another epic (stubs only).
- Server-side authorisation — implemented in E09; this ticket only consumes `/me` claims and renders the correct client-side outcome.
- Layout/workspace resolution behind `/terminal/:layoutId` (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Complete route coverage
  Given the route manifest
  When the parameterised test iterates every route ID in docs/plan/12-sitemap.md §2
  Then each ID resolves to a route element or its documented redirect, and the test fails if the sitemap gains a route that the manifest lacks

Scenario: Unauthenticated access
  Given no session cookie
  When I navigate to /terminal/abc
  Then I am redirected to /login and, after a successful login, land on /terminal/abc rather than the default route

Scenario: Viewer hits an admin route
  Given I am signed in as a Viewer
  When I navigate directly to /admin/users
  Then the router renders the 404 surface, not 403, and no admin data request is issued

Scenario: Step-up expiry
  Given I am an Owner whose step-up token is 31 minutes old
  When I navigate to /admin/keys
  Then the step-up modal is shown, and on successful TOTP re-entry the original destination loads without a full page reload

Scenario: Malformed deep-link parameter
  When I navigate to /terminal/abc?tf=99
  Then the timeframe falls back to 15, a toast explains the fallback, and the URL is rewritten to the valid value
```

## Technical notes / design
React Router data router. Loaders read a module-scoped `/me` cache populated by E10-T04 so guards do not each issue their own request. Guard composition order is fixed: `requireAuth` → `requireRole` → `requireStepUp`. The admin-404 behaviour is implemented by having `requireRole` accept a `denyAs: '403' | '404'` option, defaulting to `'403'` and set to `'404'` for the `/admin` branch.

Validators live in `apps/web/src/routes/params.ts`, one pure function per param returning `{ value, corrected: boolean, reason?: string }` so the UI can both correct and explain. Server-side re-validation is assumed for every scope-bearing param (`account`, `symbol`) — the client correction is convenience only.

In Electron the app is served from a registered `app://` protocol handler rather than `file://` so history routing, the `'self'` CSP origin and the SR-042 `Origin` check all work identically to the browser build.

## Test plan
- Unit: each param validator (valid, invalid, boundary, missing); guard composition order; `denyAs` behaviour.
- Integration: route matrix × role matrix (owner/manager/viewer × every route ID) asserting rendered outcome — this is the test that would catch a future RBAC regression.
- Contract: `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up` and the `step_up_required` problem+json shape against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- E2E: login redirect-back, viewer admin 404, step-up expiry flow.
Coverage target >=85% on `apps/web/src/routes/**` given its security relevance.

## Security notes
Implements the client half of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4 and must be reviewed with the explicit understanding that it is **not** a security control (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3). Threats: guard bypass by direct navigation (mitigated server-side; the client must still not leak admin-only data into the bundle or prefetch admin endpoints), and parameter tampering on `account`/`symbol` (server re-validates; the client must never treat a param as an authorisation grant). SR-025 step-up re-auth. `sec:review` label required. Data classification: the `/me` claims cache holds PII (display name, email) — it must not be persisted to `localStorage`.

## Accessibility notes
Route changes must move focus to the main landmark heading and announce the new route name plus the environment badge (SCR-010 a11y note: "the environment badge is announced on every route change"). The 403 and 404 surfaces use CMP-089 / CMP-090 with a heading and a named recovery action.

## Performance notes
Route-level code splitting: the admin branch and the replay branch are lazily loaded so they do not inflate the cold-start bundle (budget #10, ≤3 s). Guard loaders must not issue network requests on every navigation — they read the bootstrap cache; a stale cache is refreshed in the background, never blocking navigation.

## Observability
Metric `shell_route_change_ms` (histogram, labelled by route group). Log route-guard denials at info with the route ID and the reason, correlation-id propagated; never log the session cookie. Client denials are *not* audit events (the server-side 403 is the audited one) — this is stated in the code comment to prevent double-counting.

title: Build the hardened Electron main and preload processes (SR-110..SR-119)
body:
## Context
The Electron shell runs on the owner's trading host, alongside WSL, Docker, QuestDB and Postgres. A renderer compromise that reaches Node APIs is rated **Critical** (STRIDE E1, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9) because it is arbitrary code execution on the machine that holds the KEK. §6.11 therefore specifies a closed set of non-negotiable requirements SR-110..SR-119, and §9.4 makes `electron-hardening` a required CI check. R0 exit criterion 9 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires the shell to start with those switches enabled and to be *verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection*.

ADR-0011 remains `proposed`; per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 this work builds against Electron behind the `ShellPort` from E10-K01, so the decision stays reversible.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/desktop/src/main.ts`: app bootstrap, single-instance lock, `BrowserWindow` factory that sets, for **every** window including pop-outs: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `nodeIntegrationInWorker: false`, `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false`, `sandbox: true`, `webSecurity: true`, `allowRunningInsecureContent: false`, `experimentalFeatures: false`, `enableRemoteModule` absent (SR-110).
- `app://` custom protocol handler serving the built renderer bundle, with the SR-112 CSP applied as a response header plus a `<meta>` fallback: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' https://<tailnet-host> wss://<tailnet-host>; img-src 'self' data: blob:; worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. **No `unsafe-eval`.**
- Navigation lockdown: `will-navigate` and `setWindowOpenHandler` deny everything outside the app origin; external links open in the OS browser via `shell.openExternal` after an allow-list check.
- `apps/desktop/src/preload.ts`: `contextBridge` exposing the `ShellPort` surface as fixed, typed, allowlisted channels — **no** generic `invoke(channel, …)`, no `ipcRenderer` passthrough; arguments validated against a schema on both sides; unknown channels dropped and logged (SR-111).
- GPU flags from the E06 / ADR-0011 findings applied via `app.commandLine.appendSwitch`, recorded in a single documented list with the reason for each flag.
- `permissionRequestHandler` denying every Electron permission the app does not need (camera, microphone, geolocation, midi, notifications handled explicitly).
- KEK handle bridge: `keychain.getKekHandle()` returns an **opaque handle only** — never key material to the renderer (SR-119); the Electron main process holds no Bybit credentials and makes no exchange calls.
- Structured main-process logging into the E04 logger format, written to a local log file with redaction.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-T03 (roadmap-line items only):**
- **Auto-update channel stub**: an `UpdateChannel` abstraction behind `ShellPort` plus a version check on boot and every 15 min against the E04 build-info endpoint. Download, signature verification and install are **not implemented**, and `capabilities.autoUpdate === false` until code signing exists (SR-115); the stub exposes only `getCurrentVersion()` and `checkForUpdate()` and can never install code.
- **Single-window baseline**: the hardened `createWindow()` factory ships here with one main window plus minimal saved bounds/maximised state under the Electron `userData` directory. Multi-monitor restore, tray and pop-out windows are E15.

## Out of scope
- Window-state persistence, tray, floating windows and the auto-update stub — E10-T03.
- The CI assertion suite itself and the security review — E10-X02 (this ticket makes the build assertable; X02 makes CI enforce it).
- Code signing and a real update feed (SR-115 keeps auto-update disabled until signing exists) — R5/E48.
- Any Tauri implementation.

- Multi-monitor window-state restore, the system tray and SCR-027 floating pop-out windows - **deferred to E15** (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` section 6.2 keys pop-out state to the layout, which E15 owns).
- Any auto-update *download or install* path - blocked by SR-115 until code signing lands in R5/E48; this ticket ships the disabled channel abstraction and nothing more.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every window is hardened
  Given a packaged production build
  When any BrowserWindow is created, including a pop-out
  Then contextIsolation, sandbox and webSecurity are true, nodeIntegration and its worker/subframe variants are false, and enableRemoteModule is absent

Scenario: CSP is exactly as specified
  When the renderer loads over app://
  Then the Content-Security-Policy response header matches SR-112 verbatim, no unsafe-eval is present, and no Bybit host (api.bybit.com, api-demo.bybit.com, api.bytick.com, stream*.bybit.com) appears in any directive

Scenario: Navigation escape is blocked
  When renderer code attempts window.open or a navigation to https://example.com
  Then the navigation is denied, nothing is opened inside the app, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Preload exposes no generic IPC
  When the preload bridge is inspected at runtime
  Then window.shell exposes only the named ShellPort methods, ipcRenderer is not reachable, and invoking an unknown channel from the renderer is impossible because no channel name is caller-supplied

Scenario: KEK never reaches the renderer
  When the renderer calls keychain.getKekHandle()
  Then it receives an opaque handle string, and no code path exists that returns key material to the renderer
```

```gherkin
Scenario: The update channel cannot install code
  Given the packaged production build
  When a test exercises the update channel and requests an install
  Then capabilities.autoUpdate is false, no download is attempted, and the call is refused with UPDATE_CHANNEL_DISABLED
  And the electron-hardening job fails the build if an installer API is ever reachable (SR-115)
```

## Technical notes / design
Window options live in **one** `createWindow()` factory; a lint rule plus the E10-X02 assertion forbid `new BrowserWindow` anywhere else, so a future pop-out cannot be created with weaker options by accident.

Preload channel table is generated from the `ShellPort` interface (E10-K01) so drift is a type error. Both sides validate with a schema validator (zod or equivalent) — the main process must treat every renderer message as hostile input (STRIDE E2).

GPU flags: the exact list comes from the E06 benchmark findings; each flag is recorded in `apps/desktop/GPU_FLAGS.md` with the measurement that justifies it, because undocumented GPU flags are the classic source of "works on the reference machine only" (risk R8). `gpu.info()` exposes the probe result so the renderer can enter the `degraded-2d` path (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` F15) when WebGL2 is unavailable.

Dev-vs-prod: dev conveniences (devtools auto-open, relaxed CSP for the Vite dev server) are compiled out of production builds, and E10-X02's assertion fails the release if any leak through (SR-114, STRIDE E4).

## Test plan
- Unit: window-options factory returns the exact SR-110 option set; preload schema validation rejects malformed arguments; unknown-channel handling.
- Integration: CSP header presence and exact value on an `app://` response; navigation and `window.open` denial; permission handler denials.
- E2E (Playwright-Electron, E10-Q02): boot, assert hardening flags at runtime via the main-process test hook, assert no Bybit host in the CSP.
- CI gate: the `electron-hardening` required check (built in E10-X02).
Coverage >=85% on `apps/desktop/src` given the security weight.

## Security notes
This ticket **is** the SR-110..SR-119 implementation. Threats addressed: E1 (renderer→Node escalation), E2 (over-broad preload), E4 (dev flags leaking into release), and the SR-119 chokepoint rule that all Bybit traffic originates from the backend only. Data classification: the main process handles an opaque KEK handle (SECRET-adjacent) and session cookies within the Chromium session partition. `sec:review` label mandatory; Security engineer is a required code-owner on `apps/desktop/**` per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §9.3. Any deviation from §6.11 must be an explicit, dated accepted-risk entry signed by the Owner — never an undocumented default.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. Two indirect obligations: the window title must include the environment word so the OS window list and the screen-reader window switcher disclose Demo vs Live (CMP-215 contract), and `prefers-reduced-motion` must be forwarded from the OS to the renderer rather than being swallowed by the shell.

## Performance notes
GPU flags are the main lever on budget #1 (frame time) and budget #10 (≤3 s cold start). The main process must not block `ready-to-show`: the window is created hidden and shown on first paint to avoid a white flash and to keep the measured cold-start honest. `app.whenReady()` → "shell interactive" instrumentation is emitted here and consumed by E10-Q04.

## Observability
Main-process structured logs (E04 format) to a rotating local file with redaction — never log cookies, tokens or the KEK handle. Metrics surfaced to the renderer for the health chips: `shell_gpu_available`, `shell_main_start_ms`. Events: `shell.gpu_unavailable` when the WebGL2 probe fails.

- `E06` — GPU flag findings and the ADR-0011 interim decision.

title: Implement shell bootstrap: /me, preferences, keymap and WS system topic
body:
## Context
SCR-010 lists its data sources as `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` and the WS topics `system` and `recorder`. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` describes `/me` as "Single bootstrap call for the app shell… the UI uses this to decide which affordances to render; it is never the authorisation control itself", and pairs it with `/me/preferences` ("the app shell fetches it alongside `/me` on boot") and `/me/keymap` (used by SCR-012 and SCR-013). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2 states that **`system` is auto-subscribed**: every authenticated connection is implicitly subscribed at `auth_ok`, it carries kill-switch transitions, feature-flag changes, degraded-data notices, connectivity changes and planned-shutdown warnings, and a client may not unsubscribe from it.

Every guard, every chip and the environment badge depend on this one bootstrap; doing it once, centrally, is what keeps cold start inside budget #10.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/shell/bootstrap.ts`: a single parallel fetch of `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap` on app start, exposed as a cache the route guards (E10-T01) and chrome (E10-S01) read synchronously.
- Application of preferences at the document root: `data-theme`, `data-density`, reduced-motion override, text scale — consuming the E05 theme runtime (this ticket wires, E05 owns the tokens).
- Environment resolution: the DEMO/LIVE value comes from `/me` and the WS `system` topic only; there is **no** client-side default and the badge renders an explicit "unknown" state until the value is known (SCR-150 rule: the environment is not shown until it is actually known).
- WS `system` consumption: connect on boot, honour the auto-subscription contract, and expose a typed `SystemUpdate` store (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9) feeding CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner and the frozen/kill-switch chrome states.
- Reconnection with exponential backoff **1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s capped at 30 s with jitter** and a visible next-attempt time (SCR-152 performance note); on reconnect, restore subscriptions in priority order (private account state, focused panel, the rest).
- Offline detection driven by **actual request failure**, not only `navigator.onLine`, so a connected-but-unreachable tailnet is detected within 5 s (SCR-159 performance note).
- A `useShellState()` hook as the single read API for chrome components, so no component fetches `/me` itself.

## Out of scope
- The `/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` endpoints themselves (E09) and the WS gateway (E17).
- `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts` and `/trade-groups` consumption for the account picker — E27/E28 supply the data; E10 leaves the picker slot empty in R0.
- Recorder chip content (WS `recorder`) — E16; the chip slot exists but reports "not available" in R0.
- Preference *editing* UI (settings screens) — later settings epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One bootstrap, not many
  When the app starts
  Then exactly one request each to /api/v1/me, /api/v1/me/preferences and /api/v1/me/keymap is issued, they are issued in parallel, and no chrome component issues its own duplicate

Scenario: Environment is never guessed
  Given /me has not yet responded
  Then the environment badge renders an explicit unknown state and no DEMO or LIVE value is assumed; trading-capable affordances stay disabled until the value is known

Scenario: Preferences apply without reload
  Given the user's stored theme is high-contrast and density is compact
  When the bootstrap completes
  Then data-theme and data-density are set on the document root and the chrome renders in that theme without a page reload

Scenario: Reconnection backoff
  Given the WS connection drops
  Then reconnect attempts occur at approximately 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s with jitter, the next attempt time is displayed, and subscriptions are restored in the documented priority order on success

Scenario: Tailnet unreachable
  Given the machine reports navigator.onLine true but every request to the backend fails
  Then the offline state is detected within 5 s and SCR-159 names the condition as a tailnet/backend reachability problem rather than a generic offline message

Scenario: Bootstrap failure is explicit
  Given /me returns 500
  Then the app shows the staged boot-failure state with a named recovery action (retry, sign in again, open diagnostics) rather than an empty shell
```

## Technical notes / design
The bootstrap runs before the router renders, but with a hard ceiling: if `/me` has not resolved within 5 s the "slow boot" state is shown explaining what is waiting (SCR-150 checklist). Preferences and keymap failures are non-fatal — the app proceeds with defaults and a warning, because a broken keymap must not prevent login.

The `SystemUpdate` payload is validated against the schema generated from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 so a protocol drift surfaces as a contract-test failure rather than a silently missing chip.

Health chips update at 1 Hz from a store that is deliberately **outside** the workspace React tree, so a chip tick cannot re-render the chart subtree (SCR-010 performance note).

## Test plan
- Unit: backoff sequence and jitter bounds; offline detection from request failure; environment-unknown state machine; preference application to root attributes.
- Contract: `/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` responses against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `SystemUpdate` frames against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 — both run in the `contract` CI job.
- Integration: bootstrap failure paths (401 → login, 500 → boot-failure state, timeout → slow-boot state).
- E2E: disconnect/reconnect drill with the WS gateway stubbed, asserting subscription restore order.

## Security notes
The `/me` cache holds PII (email, display name) and role claims: it is kept in memory only, never in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, and is cleared on logout and on session revocation (a revoked session terminates the WS immediately per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5, which the client must treat as a hard logout rather than a reconnect). Role claims from `/me` are presentation hints only — never an authorisation decision (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3). Never log the payload.

## Accessibility notes
Connection-state changes announce once via `role="alert"` on transition to degraded/offline and are not re-announced on every heartbeat (CMP-076 contract). The reconnect countdown is not announced on every tick (SCR-152). Health chips expose "label: state, value" as their accessible name. The slow-boot and boot-failure states have headings and named actions.

## Performance notes
This is the critical path for budget #10 (≤3 s cold start): the three bootstrap calls are parallel, the WS connects concurrently rather than after them, and nothing blocks first paint except `/me`. Health-chip updates are throttled to 1 Hz and isolated from the workspace subtree. Target time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is ≤5 s (SCR-152).

## Observability
Metrics: `shell_cold_start_ms`, `shell_bootstrap_ms` (per call), `shell_ws_state`. Events: `ws.disconnected {reason, subscriptions}`, `ws.reconnect_attempt {attempt}`, `ws.reconnected {outageMs, gapFilled}`, `shell.offline_detected {cause}`, `shell.tailscale_unreachable`. Correlation id from the HTTP bootstrap is carried onto the WS connection per E04.

No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE decomposition of the E10 trust boundaries: B4 (renderer ↔ Electron main), the renderer ↔ backend boundary, and the OS ↔ main-process boundary (keychain, filesystem, tray, protocol handler).
- Data-flow diagram covering: bootstrap (`/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap`), WS `system`, preload IPC channels, window-state file, crash log, diagnostics bundle, `app://` protocol handler, deep-link parameters.
- Per-element STRIDE rows with likelihood, impact, rating, existing control (SR-###) and residual risk, extending `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9 rather than duplicating it. Minimum coverage of these candidate threats:
  - Spoofing: a non-app origin loaded into a window; a forged `app://` request; a malicious deep link causing an unintended action on load.
  - Tampering: window-state or crash-log file tampering influencing main-process behaviour; unsigned update (E5).
  - Repudiation: a client-side denial not being audited server-side (by design) being mistaken for an audit gap.
  - Information disclosure: diagnostics bundle leaking tokens; `/me` cache persisted to storage; crash log containing PII; DEMO/LIVE misrepresentation leading a user to act on the wrong environment.
  - Denial of service: crash loop; reconnect storm against the backend; unbounded window creation.
  - Elevation of privilege: preload bridge abuse (E2); client-side guard treated as authorisation; step-up bypass by direct navigation or restored window.
- Abuse-case list handed to E10-X03 and to the E10-Q01 charters.
- Model merged into `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9 as an extension, with any new SR requirement proposed explicitly.

## Out of scope
- Backend auth/RBAC threat modelling (E09's model) and the exchange boundary (E08's model).
- Penetration testing — R4/E43.
- Implementing controls; this ticket produces the model and the required-control list.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element has STRIDE coverage
  When the model is reviewed
  Then every data-flow element in the E10 DFD has each applicable STRIDE category either analysed or explicitly marked not-applicable with a reason

Scenario: Threats map to controls
  Then every threat rated Medium or above names an existing SR-### control or proposes a new one, with an owner and a target ticket

Scenario: The model shapes implementation
  Given the model is completed before E10-T02 merges
  Then any control it requires that E10-T02 does not yet implement is added to E10-T02's scope or filed as a blocking follow-up before E10 can close

Scenario: A threat has no adequate control
  Given a Critical or High threat with no sufficient control
  Then it is escalated to the Architect and Owner, and either a control is added or a dated accepted-risk entry is recorded with Owner sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: STRIDE-per-element over a DFD drawn in mermaid and committed alongside the model. Ratings use the likelihood/impact scale already used in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 so rows are comparable across epics. Each row records residual risk after controls, because "mitigated" without a residual statement is how risk quietly accumulates.

Particular attention to two shell-specific subtleties: (1) the client-side route guard is *not* a control and must be labelled as such in the model so a future reader does not credit it; (2) the DEMO/LIVE badge is a security control in the integrity sense — a user acting on a misrepresented environment is a real loss scenario, and it is modelled as an information-disclosure/tampering threat rather than as a UI concern.

The model's assertions are turned into testable claims: each control referenced must name the test that proves it (unit, ci-gate, e2e, manual-review), matching the "Verified by" column convention of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6. Claims without a test are flagged.

This ticket is the security artefact. Classification of E10 data: session cookie (SECRET), `/me` identity (PII), KEK handle (SECRET-adjacent, opaque), window state and crash log (INTERNAL), diagnostics bundle (INTERNAL, must be redacted before it leaves the machine).

  - `capabilities.autoUpdate === false` while signing is not operational (SR-115).
  - The preload surface exposes no generic `invoke`/`ipcRenderer` passthrough (SR-111) — asserted structurally against the generated channel table.
- **Semgrep rules**: `cv-electron-unsafe-webprefs` plus rules for `new BrowserWindow` outside the single factory, `shell.openExternal` without an allow-list check, and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in shell components.
- **ESLint**: enable `plugin:security` and `no-unsanitized` for `apps/desktop` and the shell modules, blocking at error level.
- **Security code review** of E10-T01..T04 against the E10-X01 model and the §6.11 checklist, with findings triaged.
- CODEOWNERS entry routing `apps/desktop/**`, CSP configuration and the preload to the security code-owner (`sec:review` label per §9.3).

## Out of scope
- The runtime E2E assertions — E10-Q02 (complementary: this is build-time, that is run-time; exit criterion 9 wants both).
- DAST/ZAP scanning — E03 owns the pipeline job; this ticket contributes the Electron-specific rules.
- Pen-testing — R4/E43.
- Code signing — R5/E48.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flipping a hardening flag fails CI
  Given a pull request that sets sandbox to false on any BrowserWindow
  When the electron-hardening job runs
  Then the job fails, names the offending window and the SR-110 requirement, and the PR cannot merge

Scenario: A weakened CSP fails CI
  Given a pull request adding unsafe-eval or removing frame-ancestors from the CSP
  Then the job fails naming the SR-112 directive that deviated

Scenario: A Bybit host in the CSP fails CI
  Given a pull request adding wss://stream.bybit.com to connect-src
  Then the job fails citing SR-119 and the backend-only chokepoint rule

Scenario: Dev-only affordances cannot ship
  Given a release build containing the test-only main-process hook or auto-opened devtools
  Then the job fails citing SR-114

Scenario: A new window bypasses the factory
  Given code calling new BrowserWindow outside the hardened factory
  Then the Semgrep rule cv-electron-unsafe-webprefs blocks at ERROR severity

Scenario: Security review is recorded
  When the review of E10-T01..T04 completes
  Then every finding has a severity, an SR reference and an owner, and no Critical or High finding is open when E10 closes
```

## Technical notes / design
The gate inspects the **packaged artefact**, not the source, because source-level checks miss build-time configuration and bundler output. Window preferences are asserted by launching the packaged app headlessly and reading `webContents.getLastWebPreferences()` for every created window, including one deliberately floated pop-out — so a pop-out created with weaker options is caught, which is the realistic regression.

Renderer-bundle scanning for Bybit hosts is a string scan over the emitted bundle plus the CSP, which catches both a hard-coded URL and a well-intentioned CSP addition.

Failure output names the SR requirement and links the §6.11 row, so a developer who trips the gate can self-serve the fix rather than escalating.

## Test plan
Meta-testing: the gate is validated with deliberately broken fixture builds — one per assertion — proving it fails when it should. A gate that has only ever passed is unproven; each fixture is committed and run as part of the job's own test suite.

## Security notes
This ticket is the enforcement of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.11. It closes STRIDE E1, E2, E4 and (for now, by disabling) E5. The gate itself is a supply-chain surface: it must run in a pinned, hash-locked action environment and its own configuration is code-owned by security so it cannot be quietly relaxed in a PR that also relaxes what it checks.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI and review artefact. One indirect effect: the gate asserts the window title includes the environment word, which is an a11y-relevant disclosure.

## Performance notes
The job must stay within the ≤15 min commit-to-dev pipeline budget; target ≤3 min, achieved by reusing the packaged artefact from the build job rather than rebuilding.

## Observability
Gate failures are reported with the SR reference in the CI annotation; the failure rate per SR is tracked so a frequently-tripped requirement can be re-examined (either the requirement is unclear or the code keeps drifting — both are worth knowing).

title: /settings/hotkeys persistence: migration, routes, RBAC, audit, wiring
body:
## Context
E10-S02 (#305) ships the client half of hotkey profiles: the conflict engine and the editor (SCR-113, R-202), a per-user, per-device profile store (ruling A55, #2701), and a profile-store port with an HTTP adapter written against `22`'s `/settings/hotkeys*`, **wired off** (BQ-1 of #305's ruling of record). The server half does not exist: `hotkey_profiles` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.5) is not migrated, no router serves `/settings/hotkeys*`, and `GET /me/keymap` (`services/api/candleviewer/api/me.py`) serves the contract's empty answer naming E10-S02. No other backlog ticket implements or migrates them: E30-S05, E30-S07 and E47-S08 only consume them. This Task is the server side plus the client adapter's wiring. **Contract first** (C-6.1): the `22`, `21` and `24` edits land in their own small PR before the router.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract PR first** (C-6.1, interface-first), settling what #305's reviews left open:
  - `HotkeyProfileInput` refuses unknown fields, so its generated model is `extra="forbid"` (SEC-305C-01), without breaking `HotkeyProfile`, which is `allOf[HotkeyProfileInput, {id, owner_user_id, is_active, updated_at}]` (`22` `HotkeyProfile`, :22673): flatten `HotkeyProfile` as `Watchlist` is (`22` `Watchlist`, :23239), or close the composite with `unevaluatedProperties: false`.
  - One representation for `bindings`: `21` stores a map (`{"command": ["chord"]}`) while `22`'s `HotkeyProfileInput.bindings` is an array of `HotkeyBinding`. Pick one and document the mapping.
  - `requires_arm`: `21` has a profile-level `requires_arm` column; `22` has a per-binding flag the server forces for `ArmToken`'s class, every live submit included (`22`:10644-10651). Settle the column against the per-binding flag. The contract decides the forced class (orchestrator, 2026-10-31): `ticket.submit` stays in it, and the client arm-gates the same five commands. E30-D05 §4's "`ticket.submit` requires_arm: no" is a C-row against that design, not against `22`.
  - **The `keys` grammar:** chords, plus the non-chord shapes the keymap's defaults use. 13 of the 75 defaults are not chords (4 ranges, 7 pointer chords, 2 bare modifiers), and each is accepted in its command's shape. The three locked commands (the palette on `Ctrl+K`, the two `Esc` commands) are accepted at their own defaults and refused anywhere else, and no other command may take `Esc` or `Ctrl+K`.
  - The refusals, with problem codes a client can act on:
    - `createHotkeyProfile`'s `409`: a name already taken, or a conflicting pair, named;
    - `updateHotkeyProfile`'s `412` and `409`;
    - `404` on update and delete as well as activate, for another user's id;
    - `422` on update as well as create: an unknown action, a reserved key on a command it doesn't belong to, a bare letter on a dangerous command, a shape that isn't its command's, or a scope that disagrees with the keymap's fixed context table.

    A permanent refusal must be distinguishable from a transient one (CR-305C-04).
  - **E47-S08's rule** ("a profile may not bind an action the user's role cannot perform"): settle with E47-S08's owner whether the server refuses such a binding (`422`) or stores it inert.
  - **Not conflicts:** the declared `F11` shadow (BQ-4), and two unbound commands (`keys: ""`) in one scope.
  - The audit actions `hotkey_profile.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` and `.activated` in `24` §15.5. Their state carries the profile name, the binding count and the active flag, never the full binding list.
  - Regenerate (`make gen`, then `make contracts`).
- **The command vocabulary on the server:** the API image cannot read `apps/web/src/keymap/keymap.json`. Generate a server-side copy of the action ids, contexts, each command's binding shape, the declared shadows (F11's) and the dangerous and forced sets as a checked artefact, with a freshness check, so the server validates against the one vocabulary.
- **Migration:** `hotkey_profiles` as settled in the contract PR: one Alembic revision, reversible, round-tripped (C-5.1 to C-5.5).
- **Router:** the five `/settings/hotkeys*` operations of `22` (list, create, update, delete, activate). `recordHotkeyBindingAudit` (`POST /settings/hotkey-audit`) is already served by `api/hotkey_audit.py`. Drop the five `openapi_pending` entries in `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/composition_allowlist.json`, and move the five `not_mounted` rows of `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` to mounted.
  - **RBAC:** `settings:read` and `settings:write`, scope self. Another user's profile id answers `404`.
  - **Validation:** the server checks what the client checks (the vocabulary, reserved keys, the dangerous set's bare letters, conflicts by overlapping scope), and applies the `requires_arm` rewrite.
  - **One active profile per user**, as the partial unique index says.
- **`GET /me/keymap`** serves the active profile, flattened, instead of the empty answer.
- **The client wiring** (`apps/web/src/keymap/`):
  - switch the adapter on for a user holding `settings:write`; a Viewer stays device-local (A55);
  - pull the active profile at sign-in and apply it by the import rules, so no acknowledgement carries over (CR-305BD-04);
  - define which side wins when the device and the server disagree;
  - flush on change, on `online` and at sign-in;
  - park a permanent refusal, and retry a transient one in order;
  - abort the store's requests at sign-out as well as on a user change (SEC-305C-03).

## Out of scope
- The editor UI and its hi-fi (SCR-113; E49), the arm control and the per-account arm port (E30, E30-S05), and keying under a view-as context (#304 gap 13).
- Sharing a profile between users, or importing another user's profile.
- Any change to the client's conflict rules, reserved keys or dangerous set (E10-S02's).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A profile follows its owner to another device
  Given an Owner holding settings:write has remapped "Toggle footprint" to Ctrl+Alt+F on one device
  When they sign in on a second device
  Then the active profile is read once and applied by the import rules
  And the remap applies there, with no acknowledgement carried over

Scenario: A Viewer stays on the device
  Given a Viewer, who lacks settings:write
  When they remap a command
  Then the remap applies on this device and no request reaches /settings/hotkeys

Scenario: Another user's profile does not exist
  When a user replaces, deletes or activates another user's profile id
  Then the answer is 404, and nothing changes
  And the list never names another user's profile

Scenario: The client's own default profile is accepted
  When the client saves the default keymap, every command at its default
  Then the answer is 201: the non-chord shapes and the three locked commands are accepted as they are

Scenario: A conflicting pair is refused, by name
  Given two bindings share a chord in overlapping scopes
  When the profile is saved
  Then the answer is 409 naming both commands, and nothing is stored
  But the declared F11 shadow and two unbound commands in one scope are not conflicts

Scenario: The server keeps the arm on an order submit
  When a profile is saved with requires_arm false on a placeOrder submit
  Then the server stores it as true and answers with the warning header

Scenario: Unknown fields and unknown actions are refused
  When a profile carries an unknown field or an action outside the vocabulary
  Then the answer is 422 with a problem code, and nothing is stored

Scenario: Every change is audited
  When a profile is created, replaced, deleted or activated
  Then one audit record is written with the actor, the profile id, its name and binding count

Scenario: A refusal never stalls the client
  Given the server refuses a profile permanently
  Then the client parks it, says so once, and later changes still sync
  And a transient failure retries in order
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Conflicts:** detection stays an application check at save time, as `21` §3.8.5 says. A binding's scope follows from its command's keymap context by `22`'s fixed table, and is not stored.
- **Profiles:** one active profile per user (`ux_hk_active`). Activating one deactivates the other in the same transaction.
- **The forced class:** the server's `requires_arm` rewrite covers every mutation `ArmToken` requires the token for (`22`:10644-10651), `ticket.submit` included. The client's `requiresArm` set (E10-S02) is the same five commands.
- **The client adapter** is `apps/web/src/keymap/profileStore.ts` (E10-S02 PR C). It already re-checks the user after every await and aborts on a user change.

## Test plan
- **Contract:** provider and consumer tests for every changed operation; the generated models refuse unknown fields.
- **Migration:** upgrade, downgrade and upgrade on an empty and a seeded database (`@pytest.mark.integration`).
- **Router:**
  - unit tests for validation and the rewrite;
  - integration tests against Postgres;
  - a forbidden-role case (a Viewer writing) and a cross-user (IDOR) case on every operation.
- **The vocabulary artefact:** a freshness test fails when `keymap.json` changes without a regeneration.
- **Client wiring:** vitest with a stubbed server: the pull at sign-in, the flush triggers, park against retry, abort at sign-out. No network.

## Security notes
- RBAC is server-side on every operation (C-12.4), scope self; another user's id is `404`, never `403`.
- Inbound DTOs refuse unknown fields (`extra="forbid"`).
- Audit records are append-only (C-2.9), and carry no binding list.
- The client never weakens the server's `requires_arm` rewrite, and the arm itself is decided by the server (C-2.21).
- The profile holds command ids and chords only. No secret or PII beyond the owner id (C-5.9).

## Accessibility notes
N/A on the server. The client wiring keeps the editor's messages as they are. A parked refusal is said once, politely, through the shell announcer.

## Performance notes
A profile holds about 75 bindings. It is read once at sign-in and written on change. No hot path.

## Observability
- The audit actions above.
- Structured logs with `correlationId`: the operation, the outcome and the problem code, never the binding list.
- A counter of `409`/`422` refusals by code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Contract PR (`22`, `21`, `24` §15.5) merged before the router; generated code fresh.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated; IDOR and forbidden-role cases present.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on the touched modules; migration round trip recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `21` §3.8.5 and `24` §15.5 reconciled with the build; `14` SCR-113's as-built line updated.
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: E10-S02 (#305: the client half, the keymap vocabulary and the adapter). E30-S05 consumes the active profile; this Task does not wait for it.

## Branch
`feat/e10-t05-hotkey-profiles-server`

## References
`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/settings/hotkeys*`, `HotkeyProfileInput`, `HotkeyBinding`, `ArmToken`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.5; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5; `services/api/candleviewer/api/me.py`; `apps/web/src/keymap/profileStore.ts`; #305's ruling of record (BQ-1, BQ-5), ruling A55 (#2701); E30-D05 §4 (BQ-11); #305's PR bodies (PR B, PR C) for SEC-305C-01, SEC-305C-03, CR-305C-04 and CR-305BD-04.
